newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar makes sleepy start in holiday-thinned Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar makes sleepy start in holiday-thinned Asia.

text.p: 0100 GMT 2400 GMT NYK CLOSE
The dollar made a sluggish
start in Asian morning trade on Tuesday as the absence of Tokyo
players severely hampered activity.
Dealers said the dollar maintained a strong undertone after
the weekend Group of Seven (G7) meeting suggested overall
satisfaction with its current levels, but the market lacked
momentum to push it higher.
Comments by Japan Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and Bank of Japan (BOJ) chief Yasuo Matsushita, speaking in Washington, had little impact on the market, dealers said.
Mitsuzuka said the G7 members shared a concern about
excessive currency movements and would cooperate to act properly
in forex markets.
Matsushita repeated that the BOJ would maintain its current
monetary policy of putting emphasis on ensuring economic
recovery for the time being.
"Until the BOJ says something different, or comes in and intervenes, or lets the call rate squeeze higher, there's going to be decent interest to buy the dollar on dips," a European bank dealer said.

"But maybe the market is learning that speed kills. And if they don't go too fast, they can get away with (pushing the dollar higher)," he said, adding that Mitsuzuka's comment could be read as a veiled threat.
He said the market was long on dollars but the G7 communique had given added impetus to its bullish mood.
"People are still bullish but they'd rather not buy the dollar until they have a clearer indication from the data tonight," another European bank dealer said.
A slew of U.S. economic data, including the quarterly employment cost index, are due from 1230 GMT.
Dealers said the dollar was likely to keep to a range of 1.7280-1.7350 marks and 126.50-126.90 yen during Asian trade.
-- Sonali Desai (65-8703090)
